To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the timing of inhibition is delayed relative to excitation and that this delay is a major determinant of the IID selectivity observed in LSO cells.
(a) the latency of inhibition is longer than that of excitation and (b) the latency of the inhibitory input can be shortened by increasing the sound level to the inhibitory side.

the latency of inhibition in the LSO is delayed by several hundred microseconds relative to the latency of exciation and that this delay accounts for a substantial portion of the variation of selectivity to IIDs among LSO cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes information from the two ears in order to determine the location of a sound.
the role of the auditory brainstem in the localization of sounds in space, and in particular with the processing of the cues used by animals to localize low-frequency sounds.
understanding the mechanisms that underlie the ability of bats to locate sound sources in three dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural delays in the lateral superior olivary nucleus shape the selectivity of LSO neurons to interaural time and intensity differences.

the latency of the inhibitory input to LSO neurons is longer than the latency for the excitatory input, and that the latency difference can account for a significant proportion of the variability in the selectivity of the neurons.
a neural delay of inhibition is a significant contributor to the variation in the selectivity to IIDs of LSO cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LSO is a very sensitive detector of interaural time differences.
the LSO is the site of the first neural computation that extracts IID information from the binaural cues.
, in the LSO, the neural delays of excitation and inhibition, together with the pattern of innervation and the relative intensities of the two inputs, determine the selectivity to IIDs.
